bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Plastic Surgeon Salary Landscape

When researching a **plastic surgeon salary** in Australia, you'll find that these medical specialists are among the highest earners. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) data reported by, plastic surgeons work an average of 51 hours per week and have median weekly earnings well above the national average. For context, the ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, while all employees (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week.

But how does that translate into an hourly rate or annual salary? Whether you're a surgeon negotiating a contract or a practice manager setting pay rates, understanding the conversion from hourly to annual—and factoring in casual loading and superannuation—is essential. This guide walks you through the process using the latest Fair Work and ATO figures.

### Hourly to Annual Conversion: The Formula

The basic formula is straightforward:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a standard full-time week of 38 hours (the benchmark used in the National Minimum Wage), the calculation becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52**

For example, if a plastic surgeon earns $150 per hour:
- Annual gross = $150 × 38 × 52 = $296,400
- Fortnightly gross = $150 × 38 × 2 = $11,400 (or weekly × 2)

This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. In reality, surgeons often work more than 38 hours—the ABS reports an average of 51 hours per week for plastic surgeons. If you work 51 hours, the annual figure changes: $150 × 51 × 52 = $397,800. Always use your actual hours for a more accurate estimate.

### The Role of Casual Loading and Super

Our [pay guides](/blog) cover minimum award rates, but plastic surgeons are typically not covered by modern awards like the Medical Practitioners Award [MA000031] unless employed in a public hospital or similar setting. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for that award, but most surgeons operate under enterprise agreements or as independent contractors.

**Casual loading** of 25% applies to casual employees under many awards. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees, but casuals get $33.05 per hour (including 25% loading). However, plastic surgeons are rarely casual; they are usually permanent employees or self-employed. If you are a casual surgeon (unlikely), you would add 25% to your base hourly rate. Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you check a box to add casual loading on top of your base rate—never type a rate that already includes loading.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% from 1 July 2026, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a surgeon earning $296,400 annually, super would be 12% of $270,830 = $32,499.60 (since earnings above that cap don't attract compulsory super). Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional contribution by your employer. Learn more on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Tax Considerations

Once you have your annual gross, you need to estimate tax. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a gross of $296,400, the tax would be approximately:
- $0 on first $18,200
- $4,020 on next $26,800 (15%)
- $27,000 on next $90,000 (30%)
- $20,350 on next $55,000 (37%)
- $47,880 on remaining $106,400 (45%)
- Total tax ≈ $99,250, plus Medicare $5,928 = $105,178

Take-home pay would be around $191,222 per year, or $3,677 per week. These are estimates only; use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised calculation.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/) is designed for anyone with an hourly rate. Enter your base hourly rate (e.g., $150), and the tool calculates annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. If you are a casual employee, check the casual loading box to add 25% on top. The tool assumes a 38-hour week by default, but you can adjust hours. It also estimates super and tax using the latest ATO and Fair Work data.

Remember: the results are estimates. They assume consistent hours, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. For precise figures, consult a tax professional or your employer.

### Comparing with National Benchmarks

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). A plastic surgeon earning $150 per hour is earning over 5.5 times that rate. The ABS average weekly earnings for all employees ($1,579.20) is about $41.56 per hour for a 38-hour week. Plastic surgeons far exceed that, reflecting the extensive training and responsibility.

For more detailed award rates, visit the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database or the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog). Our [reference tables](/data) also provide quick comparisons.

### Final Thoughts

Whether you're calculating a **plastic surgeon salary** for a job offer or your own practice, the hourly-to-annual formula is your starting point. Factor in actual hours worked, casual loading if applicable, and super paid on top. Use our tools to get a clear picture of your gross and net pay. And always check your specific award or agreement—the Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission are your authoritative sources.
